name: ARENA_STRETCH
summary: Ellipse dial: 0.75 spends three quarters of the spare vertical room stretching the arena; 0 restores an exact circle.
detail: Declared `let`, so it is settable from the console, but resize() must run again for it to take effect. AY (the vertical radius multiplier) is 1+(clamp(vBox/R,1,ARENA_MAX_Y)-1)*min(1,ARENA_STRETCH). Raising it toward 1 widens ring spacing on tall phones (the playtest complaint it answers); lowering it toward 0 shrinks every orbit back to the width-bound circle.

name: ARENA_MAX_Y
summary: Hard ceiling of 1.55 on the arena's vertical radius multiplier, so a very tall screen stops before the ellipse reads as an egg.
detail: Only binds when vBox/R exceeds 1.55, i.e. on unusually tall viewports. Raising it lets tall phones stretch further and pushes ring spacing up; lowering it toward 1 collapses toward a circle regardless of ARENA_STRETCH. Caught by check.mjs's doc-staleness guard (name is 5+ chars and the value is a plain literal), so any docs/**.md paragraph naming ARENA_MAX_Y must state 1.55.

name: resize() arena box (topLim / botLim / hBox / R floor)
summary: Arena radius R is solved from the free box: 150u of HUD above, 74u of shield button below, 30u of side clearance, floored at 52px.
detail: topLim=safeTop+150u, botLim=H-safeBot-74u, vBox=max(40,(botLim-topLim)/2), hBox=W/2-30u, R=max(52,min(hBox,vBox)). The 30u side clearance is sized for the comet plus a full three-shield stack (15u sprite at 1.86x = 28u). Shrinking 150u or 74u grows the arena and risks the HUD colliding with the outer ring; growing them shrinks every orbit. Replaced a flat min(W,usableH)*0.31 that left 74px of dead margin in portrait and overlapped in landscape.

name: u (the scale unit)
summary: Every drawn size is a multiple of u = clamp(min(W,H)/420, 0.75, 1.3), so one number scales the whole board across devices.
detail: Recomputed on every resize() before the arena box is solved. Raising the 1.3 ceiling makes everything larger on tablets; raising the 420 reference makes everything smaller everywhere. The sprite cache is keyed on u (sprU), so changing it forces a re-bake on the next resize.

name: ARENA_PARALLAX
summary: A/B dial (1.0) for whether the orbit stack rides the camera dolly by depth; 0 restores the flat, pinned stack exactly.
detail: Declared `let`. The offset is a pure function of radius via depthOf(r)=min(1.35,r/R), so every object standing on an orbit gets exactly that orbit's offset through posAt() and nothing can come unstuck from its track. Known approximation: stored positions (the nova front's centre, trail points, particle birthplaces) carry the offset that was live when taken — sub-pixel at this amplitude, and no hit test reads them.

name: PARA_K
summary: The arena's parallax swing as a multiple (1.15) of the backdrop dolly's, so the outer orbit leans against a fixed hub lamp.
detail: Raising it exaggerates the differential between the outer orbit and the depth-0 hub; lowering it toward 0 flattens the stack onto one plane. Covered by check.mjs's doc-staleness guard, so any docs paragraph naming PARA_K must state 1.15.

name: RAD_OFF / RAD_BH / RAD_BAKE / RADII
summary: Four-slot ring radius fractions of R: normal play is [1,0.76,0.545,0] (three rings), black hole re-spaces to [1,0.80,0.62,0.45].
detail: Ring 0 is the OUTERMOST; a new ring is a higher index further in, so existing rings never move when one appears. RADII is live and eased between RAD_OFF and RAD_BH — the black hole re-spaces the whole annulus rather than squeezing a fourth ring into the shipped gaps (the rejected version put the fourth at f=0.33, where hitTol makes one shard block 35.7 degrees). RAD_BAKE is what the halo sprites are baked at, so easing the radii costs no re-bake. radiusOf(i) is R*RADII[i].

name: hitTol / sep
summary: A shard's hit half-width is 18.5u radians over its ring radius, so the same object blocks twice the angle on the innermost ring.
detail: hitTol(ring)=(18.5*u)/radiusOf(ring); sep(ring,k)=k*hitTol(ring). Spawn clearances are multiples of the hit width rather than flat radians, which is what makes them correct on every ring and screen size (both terms carry the same u/radius factor). Any k above 2 leaves a real gap; k=3.5 reproduces what ring 0 always had. Star and mirror pickup use a separate flat 22u tolerance.

name: farFromAll clearance arguments
summary: Spawn separation constants: stars use minP 0.45 / sep k 2.8 / 3.9, orbs use 0.6 / 3.2 / 3.0, with 14 and 24 placement attempts.
detail: farFromAll(a,ring,minP,minSpike,minStar,behind) rejects a candidate angle. spawnStar tries 14 times at (0.45, sep(ring,2.8), sep(ring,3.9)); spawnPow tries 24 times at (0.6, sep(ring,3.2), sep(ring,3.0)). Raising the sep multipliers thins the board by making placement fail more often — measured mean was 6.2 shards on a board whose cap was 8, so placement failure, not shardCap, is what actually limits density.

name: BEHIND_MIN / behindPad
summary: Nothing spawns in the arc immediately behind the comet: max(0.45 rad, 0.16s of travel at current speed), and gates are exempt.
detail: behindPad() returns 0 while any gate segment is live (phase<2) so the one formation that demands a reversal can never be the one that punishes it. The pad is a TIME, not an angle, floored at BEHIND_MIN, so the guarantee does not shrink as the game speeds up. This asymmetric exclusion replaced a symmetric read of G.angle, which gave a camper a permanent sanctuary: any oscillation arc narrower than 1.1 rad was provably unreachable by every static formation.

name: GATE_ESCAPE
summary: A gate is only placed if the reversal it forces opens onto 1.1 radians of clear run on some ring; otherwise the formation is downgraded.
detail: reverseEscape(minArc) walks every ring measuring distance to each live shard along the POST-reversal heading and returns true if any ring is clear for minArc. 1.1 rad is also the width of the sanctuary a camper could occupy under the old symmetric spawn exclusion, which is why BEHIND_MIN now follows travel instead of position. Lowering it lets the game ship traps; raising it makes gates rarer on a busy board.

name: SKY_BANDS
summary: Four backdrop palettes (bg gradient, three nebula tints, limb colour) keyed to ladder milestones so world change and rule change arrive together.
detail: Every band keeps the field at or below the opening band's luminance and stays out of the red family — the sky must never compete with a shard for the word 'danger'. skyI is written by the game rather than read from G, because the first bake runs before G exists. Which tier rungs select a band is T_SKY, derived by name from TIERS. Changing a bg stop changes the whole 2D fallback backdrop; changing limb changes the arena's rim light.

name: SKY_SWELL / SKY_FLOW / SKY_RATE
summary: Dead backdrop-motion dials (0.08 / 0.008 / 0.20): the comment calls them the whole feel of the sky, but nothing in the repository reads them.
detail: The only occurrences of these identifiers anywhere in src/, tools/ and docs/ are the comment block describing them and their own declaration line. The sky's motion now comes from GL_MOTION multiplied by each world's own `motion` field. A session that edits these will change nothing; the surprising part is that the comment above them still reads as authoritative.

name: WORLDS
summary: Eight authored celestial portraits (DRIFT TIDE DUSTLANE GLASS EMBERFALL VEIL GRID DEEPFIELD), each 19 numeric fields the sky shader interpolates between.
detail: Fields: n, arc placement (x,y,lean,width), shape (bend,reach,grain,gain), planet (px,py,size,tilt), surface (flatten,rock,clouds,sun), plus star, motion and three RGB triples (tint, rim, dust). skyMix() lerps neighbour worlds with a smoothstep over the last 20% of each world's span, so the journey morphs continuously rather than cutting. Position and scale are fractions of viewport height. All texture is generated; no outside artwork is required, though SKY_ART_WORLDS supplies optional paintings by the same order.

name: ORB_PER_WORLD
summary: Seven completed orbits buy the next world; each lap adds 1/7 to G.skyW whether or not it was star-fed.
detail: At a fed orbit every ~9s this is a new sky roughly every minute of clean play. It exists because an orbit used to pay only into a number in the corner, so the mechanic was invisible ('many people have complained they didnt even know they were supposed to do orbits'). Lowering it makes the journey cheap and the reward routine; raising it makes worlds rare and the trickle (ORB_WORLD_SECS) dominant. fxcheck.mjs reads ORB_PER_WORLD out of the game to assert the sky advances by 1/7 per orbit.

name: ORB_WORLD_SECS
summary: The trickle underneath the journey: 150 seconds of any play advances one world, so a struggling player's sky is never frozen.
detail: Deliberately far slower than the orbit route — the point is that orbiting is how you travel, not one of two ways. Lowering it toward the orbit rate would make orbits pointless as a travel mechanic; raising it strands a player who cannot close a lap. Not covered by the doc-staleness guard, because it is the second name in a multi-declaration and the guard's regex only catches the first.

name: LEVEL_HOME
summary: Each level's opening world as a FLOOR on the journey: [0,1,2,3,4,7] — DRIFT, TIDE, VEIL, GLASS, EMBERFALL, DEEPFIELD.
detail: Applied as Math.max against a journey that never goes backwards, which is why the table must climb. It previously read [0,1,5,3,2,7]: levels 4 and 5 asked for worlds already behind level 3's floor, so three of six levels had dead entries and EMBERFALL and GLASS were never seen as an opening image in a real run from level 1. VEIL cannot move — it is GRID's bright neighbour and the sky-brightness gate fails without it — so VEIL and GRID are travelled THROUGH rather than assigned. Indices are into WORLDS.

name: SKY_ARENA_CALM
summary: 0.62 of contrast moderation in the annulus the orbits occupy, so a shard stays readable against a hot sky; 0 gives the unmoderated backdrop.
detail: One of the two renderer controls CLAUDE.md names explicitly. It replaced an outright ban on red in the sky: hue is free, contrast behind the rings is not. Lowering it toward 0 lets EMBERFALL burn behind the orbits and puts the 'red means danger' contract at risk; raising it flattens the backdrop inside the ring band. implementation.md discusses a historical 0.10 and 0.34 in one paragraph and states the current 0.62 in another, which is exactly the shape check.mjs's staleness guard allows.

name: SKY_ART_WORLDS
summary: Eight optional painted backdrops keyed to the WORLDS order, each with a vertical crop focus between 0.25 and 0.36.
detail: skyArtImage falls back to 'nebula-arena' and then to the procedural sky if the host supplies no texture, so the runtime renders without any of them. focus is the vertical crop centre used only in landscape (portrait pins 0.5). skyArtPlate overscans by 1.045 so the illustrated edge stays outside the moving camera. Keys: drift-ringed-world, tide-world, dustlane-world, glass-world, emberfall-world, veil-world, grid-world, deepfield-world.

name: SCENE_RANK / SCENE_TINT
summary: One authored scene event at a time: rank 1 orbit, 2 for the calm orbs, 3 for nova/hyper/drop — a higher rank interrupts a live lower one.
detail: scenePulse refuses to replace a live event of strictly higher rank, so a nova cannot be stepped on by a shield pickup. SCENE_TINT gives each kind an RGB triple the shader reads as its accent. The orbit accent is deliberately weaker than the rest — its strength is min(0.60, 0.28+0.065*lapStreak) while everything else runs the full envelope. Attack is 0.18s smoothstep; the default span is 1.8s, floored at 0.35.

name: nebulas
summary: Dead six-cloud drift table with incommensurate LFO periods; declared once and never read, superseded by the GL/2D world sky.
detail: Its comment argues for six clouds on incommensurate periods rather than three ('three blobs on near-identical LFOs read as three blobs sliding'), which is real reasoning about a field that no longer exists in the draw path. The identifier appears exactly once in the repository.

name: MOTES
summary: Dead 44-entry dust-mote table built at load with radii stored as multiples of ring 0; nothing in the repository reads it.
detail: Built once at module load so a resize never reshuffles the motes, which is the right design for a table that is drawn — but the identifier occurs only on its declaration and its own fill loop. Radii span 1.08 to 1.75 of ring 0; drift rate 0.5-1.6 in either direction; size 0.5-1.1.

name: FLK
summary: Sixteen random values baked at load for the comet's furnace flicker, sampled at 24Hz so the flicker never costs a Math.random() per frame.
detail: Read as FLK[(G.t*24|0)&15] at two draw sites — the comet core and the hypernova glow. Reduced-motion substitutes a constant (0.6 and 0.5 respectively). Growing the table lengthens the flicker's period before it repeats; changing 24 changes the flicker rate.

name: buildStarField tiers
summary: 173 background stars in three tiers (104 dim, 54 mid, 15 bright with halos), generated once in normalised space so resizing never reshuffles the sky.
detail: Tier rows are {n, r-range, alpha-range, colour, halo}. Only the brightest 15 carry halos. A separate 22-star bgStars array with its own twinkle is built in resize(). Raising tier counts costs draw time on every frame; raising the alpha ranges risks competing with the arena for attention.

name: MASTER
summary: Bus makeup gain of 2.15 after the limiter; measured, not guessed — 2.6 put the nova cascade three samples over full scale.
detail: The old layer peaked at 0.138 on the busiest moment in the game, so ~86% of the headroom was unused, which is why it sounded thin on a phone rather than clipped. Raising it toward 2.6 clips the loudest cascade; lowering it gives back the headroom that was the original defect. It feeds a WaveShaper soft clip (tanh(x*1.25)/tanh(1.25), 1024 points, 2x oversample) so a stacked moment saturates instead of tearing.

name: buildBus node values
summary: Fixed audio bus: limiter -16dB/knee 6/ratio 12, band 0.72, reverb send 0.20, dub delay dotted-eighth at 104bpm with 0.42 feedback.
detail: Signal path is voice -> dry/send -> world|verb -> limiter -> makeup(MASTER) -> soft clip -> out; the bed runs bedDuck -> hole -> pump -> band. `band` at 0.72 leaves headroom in ordinary flight. The player's own instrument bypasses bedDuck AND hole through `perf`, with a +3dB peaking bell at 1.5kHz (Q 0.9) — the most efficient band on a 15mm phone driver. Reverb is a convolver over a 1.6s generated impulse, highpassed at 420Hz and lowpassed at 3200Hz to keep the room dark. Delay: 1.2s max, (60/104)*0.75s tap, 0.42 feedback, 1100Hz lowpass per repeat, 0.55 out.

name: BPM / SPB / STEPS
summary: One fixed tempo for the whole game: 104 BPM, SPB = 60/104 s per beat, and a 32-step loop of four bars counted in eighths.
detail: Nothing speeds up and nothing changes key mid-level; what changes inside a level is how much of the arrangement is heard and which section is playing. The tempo is load-bearing for the dub delay (a dotted eighth at 104), BLINK (SPB*2), SAUCER_CHG (one beat), MIRROR_BEATS and the hypernova (both counted in beats), and PAY = 2*STEPS. Changing BPM retimes every one of those at once.

name: CH (live chord table)
summary: The four-chord row everything reads, overwritten by applySect from PROG or PROGB; it ships holding level 1's verse (Am F C G).
detail: CH[0][0] is read as 'the level's tonic' by roughly twenty-five call sites — the snare body, fireDrop, the braam, the star-dive floor, the black hole and half the SFX layer — which is why row slot 0 must always be the i chord in both PROG and PROGB, and why the chorus rotation lives in CHOFF instead. Declared with real values rather than empty because buildBed retunes from CH[0] before a level is ever started. musiccheck.mjs enforces the tonic-slot rule.

name: ARP / CNT
summary: The live arp contour (8 even eighths, degrees 0-4) and the counter-line degrees [7,5,4,5,7,8,7,5], both indices into PENT.
detail: ARP tops out at degree 4 (784Hz at level 1) on purpose: the player's own instrument floor is 784, and a boundary only reads as a boundary if the band actually stops below it. ARP is overwritten per section by applySect from ARPL (verse) or ARPBL (chorus). CNT is indexed as CNT[((i/4)|0)%CNT.length] and sounded an octave down.

name: STARRUN
summary: The hypernova's sixteen-sixteenth line [4,5,6,7,5,6,7,8,6,7,8,9,7,8,9,10] — four ascending cells that climb and wrap instead of resolving.
detail: Indices into PENT, so it transposes with the level's key and stays consonant against every chord in either section. Degrees 4-10 sit ABOVE the band's degree-4 arp ceiling: the star is the one voice in the game meant to be on top of the arrangement. Restated for as long as the hypernova lasts.

name: LAYER_AT / LAYER_NAME
summary: The score-anchored layer ladder: rhythm at 600, melody at 1400, deep bass at 2400, high notes at 3600, each announced by name.
detail: Read as G.score >= LAYER_AT[n] at four scheduling sites and once in startGame to restore G.layerN. Lowering the thresholds gives a short run the full arrangement and removes the reason to keep scoring; raising them means most runs never hear layers 3 and 4. The RIFF and SOLO tunes this ladder used to declare inline were deleted when the per-level RIFFL/SOLOL arrived.

name: PAY / S16 / PAYLEN / PAYREST
summary: The Starfall release is PAY=32 eighth-steps = 4 bars = PAYLEN 9.23s, with PAYREST 0 so earning one is never taxed by a cooldown.
detail: A step is an eighth, so PAY=32 is four bars, PAYLEN=PAY*(SPB/2)=9.23s, and payEnd is PAYLEN+0.6. The surrounding comment still says PAY = 2 x STEPS and 'Eight bars, 18.46s' — both stale, since STEPS is also 32. PAYREST was 20s, which with the old section put a second drop 38.5s after the first, beyond what most runs survive; dropcheck.mjs now asserts PAY===32 && PAYREST===0 and calls it a four-bar release. PAYLEN is also the Starfall's own duration and its invulnerability window.

name: HOOKL
summary: Six per-level payoff hooks, 8 bars x 16 sixteenths of PENT degrees (-1 = rest); bars 2, 3 and 6 are silent and belong to the player.
detail: The RHYTHM is shared across all six on purpose — those 3+3+2 accent positions are the hook's signature, they keep it clear of ARP's straight eighths, and they are the grid the response bars answer against. Four different rhythms would be four different pieces of music; six melodies over one rhythm is a game with a tune. Only the pitches move. Bar 7 is always a written descent landing one eighth before the ordinary loop resumes. musiccheck rejected an attempt to express HEAT DEATH's cooling by removing notes from the grammar, so the energy leaves through pitch instead.

name: HOOKBL / HOOKGL / HOOKBGL
summary: A second ending for bars 4-5 (32 slots per level) played on every other section, plus the derived note-gap tables for both hooks.
detail: 32 slots because the two bars sit over different chords. The accents keep the 3+3+2 grammar or the bars stop reading as the same tune. hookGaps counts sixteenths to the next non-rest, wrapping on the table's own length, so a note can be as long as the gap it owns; HOOKGL and HOOKBGL are HOOKL and HOOKBL mapped through it. One derivation replaced two hand-written copies.

name: ANSWERL
summary: Six 16-slot answering melodies, one per level, that fill the hook's silent bars automatically — including for a player who never taps.
detail: Replaced input-response bars that only sounded if the player played them. Degrees are PENT indices with -1 as rest, same vocabulary as HOOKL.

name: PENT / PENT_BASE
summary: A 14-degree minor pentatonic from A4 440Hz to 2637Hz; PENT is rescaled by LV[].key on every level change, PENT_BASE keeps the original.
detail: Every sound effect in the game speaks through PENT, which is why every chord in PROG and PROGB must be diatonic to its level's natural minor: the pentatonic contains the tonic, third, fourth, fifth and seventh, so a borrowed major dominant would put a raised leading tone a semitone under the pentatonic's seventh in every effect the game has. musiccheck.mjs cross-checks LV[].key against PROG's tonic pitch class. The player's own instrument floor is PENT[4] = 783.99.

name: PROG
summary: Six verse progressions, one per level, four chords of four absolute frequencies each; row slot 0 is always the level's i chord.
detail: Am F C G / Gm F Eb Cm / Fm Ab Cm Db / Ebm Cb Db Ebm / Dbm Gbm Cb Fb / Bm Em F#m G. Keys walk the whole-tone scale down (A G F Eb Db B), one full lap, which is why there are six levels and not seven. Roots are written absolutely and level 6's tonic is the literal 61.74Hz floor; the register turnaround happens in the arrangement (level 6's bassline rides ch[1] an octave up) and in subF(), which octave-doubles anything under 40Hz. Level 4 crashed on arrival before this row existed — PROG, ARPL, RIFFL and SOLOL are all indexed by G.level-1.

name: PROGB
summary: Six chorus progressions — the horizontal form axis; playing hot lifts the record into its chorus at the next four-bar seam.
detail: Am F G Em / Gm Gm Eb F / Fm Fm Ab Eb / Ebm Gb Bbm Abm / Dbm Bbb Fb Cb / Bm D A Em. Every row's chord 0 is still the i chord; the walk order is rotated by CHOFF so a chorus can open off-tonic while CH[0] never stops being the tonic those twenty-five readers assume. Shapes are studied from Kavinsky (Nightcall, Odd Look, Protovision): the lift is a rotation, never a key change, and the records' major V is the one chord this game cannot borrow because the SFX pentatonic would rub its raised seventh.

name: CHOFF
summary: Where each level's chorus walk begins in its PROGB row: [1,2,0,3,1,1] — the rotation that lets a chorus open off-tonic.
detail: The walk is row[(bar+CHOFF[level-1])%4]. This exists so that PROGB slot 0 can stay the i chord (which CH[0][0]'s ~25 readers depend on) while the section still starts somewhere else — Nightcall's chorus withholds the tonic for three bars. musiccheck.mjs derives the expected bass root through the rotation, not from the raw row.

name: CHOR_HOLD
summary: An earned chorus holds twelve bars (~28s) after the hot state lapses, so the section reads as a section rather than a flicker.
detail: PLAY.heat gains +0.26 a tap against 0.34/s of decay, so it collapses within a second of the player's hands going quiet — the chorus used to go with it and settle back at the very next seam. Entry is untouched and still has to be earned; this governs only the exit. musiccheck reads CHOR_HOLD out of the game (holdSteps = (CHOR_HOLD+8)*8) rather than hardcoding it, and asserts entry and exit separately.

name: SEVB
summary: The chorus colour tone: each chorus chord's own stacked-third seventh, one per bar an octave up, indexed like PROGB rows.
detail: m7 on the minor chords, maj7 on III and VI, and on VII a minor seventh over a major triad — the mode's dominant-shaped chord with no raised leading tone anywhere. Diatonic by construction, since a third above the chord's fifth never leaves the scale. musiccheck matches scheduled voices against SEVB[level-1] doubled and fails if fewer than three of the four bars fire.

name: ARPL
summary: Six per-level verse arp contours, eight even eighths of PENT degrees 0-4, copied into the live ARP by applySect(0).
detail: Every row starts on degree 0 and never exceeds 4, which is what keeps the band below the player's 784Hz floor. Level 1's row is identical to the shipped ARP literal.

name: ARPBL
summary: Six per-level chorus arp contours on the same even-eighth grid and the same 0-4 ceiling, so the section change reads melodically too.
detail: Chosen to differ from ARPL at enough positions that musiccheck can distinguish them: the check asserts a 16-slot run following ARPBL's contour and none following ARPL's while the chorus is playing (the rows differ at five positions).

name: RIFFL
summary: Six per-level riff lines, 16 sixteenths of PENT degrees with -1 as rest — the layer-1 tune, different on each level rather than transposed.
detail: Indexed by G.level-1 alongside PROG, ARPL and SOLOL; all four stopped at three rows before level 4 existed, which crashed the level on arrival. No harness reads RIFFL by name.

name: SOLOL
summary: Six per-level afterglow solos, 32 sixteenths of PENT degrees; REDSHIFT's sinks a degree per cell and HEAT DEATH's has the widest gaps.
detail: Sits above the arp ceiling (degrees 5-12), which is deliberate — the solo is meant to be heard on top. Same indexing hazard as RIFFL: G.level-1 with no clamp at the declaration site.

name: TIGHT
summary: The rhythm judging window is 32ms of deviation from the player's learned bias; the STEADY HAND upgrade widens it to 45ms.
detail: The window judges CONSISTENCY, not absolute accuracy: a phone adds 30-50ms between finger and JS event, so a player reliably 60ms late still gets credit while arbitrary tapping has no stable bias to deviate from. Three tiers: CLIMB (tight against the QUARTER, ~11% for a random tap), HOLD (tight against the sixteenth only — keeps the chain, does not climb), SLIP (one rung, never the chain, never points). Widening TIGHT re-opens the random-walk-to-x8 exploit the quarter anchor was introduced to close.

name: CUE / cueTone
summary: Tonal payloads are quantised onto the sixteenth grid; a taken slot cascades to the next sixteenth, capped one beat out so a burst compresses.
detail: The caller keeps its instant transient (feel) and hands the tonal payload to cueTone, so a fast ember chain comes out as an actual sixteenth-note run. The earliest slot is max(gridNear(), now+0.012). If no context or no scheduler is running, fn(0) fires immediately — the game is never silent-by-quantisation.

name: DIST (guitar waveshaper)
summary: A 512-point tanh(x*5) curve baked once at load, with a 2.2 pre-gain, so a distorted note costs no more than a clean one.
detail: Used by gtr(): three detuned sawtooths (f, f-9 cents, f*1.5) into the shaper, then a lowpass sweeping 3400Hz down to 1200Hz over the note, 0.4 to the reverb send and 0.3 to the dub delay. Raising the tanh drive squares the tone; lowering it toward 1 makes the guitar clean.

name: HOOKL bars 4-7 (unreachable)
summary: payoffStep only ever reaches HOOKL bars 0-3, so half of every authored hook — including bar 7's written descent — never sounds.
detail: In payoffStep, n = PAY - MU.pay runs 0..31 and pb = n>>3, so pb is 0..3 and ix = pb*16 + s16 never exceeds 63. HOOKL rows are 128 slots (8 bars). Bars 2 and 3 are the answer bars (answer = pb===2||pb===3) and late = pb>=2, so the section is: statement, statement, answer, answer. The `pb!==7` guards and the bar-7 descent are dead code. musiccheck's accent grammar still reads bars 0,1,4,5,7 and enforces a signature on three bars the runtime cannot play. Restoring the eight-bar section means PAY=64, not editing the tables.

name: dl() difficulty clock
summary: Every pressure term keys off one number: dl() = level floor + a ramp of 0.55x for 80s then 1:1, plus up to 40s of score nudge.
detail: dl() returns LV[level-1].dl0 + (a<80 ? a*0.55 : 44+(a-80)) where a = (age()+min(G.diff*0.22,40))*MD().clock. Each level re-runs the gentle opening ramp from its own floor. Scoring well nudges the clock forward, capped at 40 difficulty-seconds, so playing well can never accelerate you into the wall. Returns 0 during an intro and LAB_DL in the lab. Slowing this one number eases speed, shard cap, arrival rate, warning length, the tier ladder and the finish line together and in the proportions they were tuned in — which is why a second difficulty mode is a clock rate rather than a second curve.

name: SPEED_MAX / speedAt
summary: Comet speed opens at 1.30 rad/s and climbs 1.30 + 1.70(1-e^(-dl/190)) plus 0.0015 per dl past 250, capped at 4.2.
detail: Half a run is spent below 2.0. The exponential is within 0.2 of its ceiling by ~4 minutes, so the linear tail past dl 250 is what stops a long run settling onto a plateau where the only deaths come from lapses of attention. The mode trim scales the whole curve INCLUDING the ceiling. Raising SPEED_MAX makes the late game faster than any telegraph was tuned for; lowering the 1.30 opener makes the first orbits a glide.

name: warnTime
summary: A shard's telegraph runs 2.35s at dl 0, decays to a 1.00s plateau, then eases to a hard floor of 0.86s over HEAT DEATH's first minutes.
detail: max(0.86, min(max(1.0, 2.35-d*0.0042), 1.0-(d-examDl)*0.00078)) * mode.warn, where examDl = LV[LEVEL_MAX-2].end = the last level's floor (dl 610). Anchored to the LV boundary rather than a literal, because the previous ease ran dl 460-640 and put 78% of the decay inside REDSHIFT — a teaching level — while leaving HEAT DEATH flat. At the fastest speeds 0.86s is still about three radians of travel between arming and lethal, which is the whole reason the floor exists.

name: shardCap
detail: The front starts at ONE: the first threat arrives alone, and pairs only exist once the tap has had something real to answer. The 10 and 11 steps were nudged from 420/540 to 445/575 so a density step never lands inside the DIVERS (395) or NARROWS (520) lesson window. Nothing below dl 420 moves — levels 1-3 are tuned and most runs end there. Multiplied by mode.cap (floored at 1) and by bhDensity() during the black hole's challenge phase. Placement failure, not this cap, is what actually limits density: measured mean was 6.2 shards on a board whose cap was 8.

name: spawnGap
summary: Seconds between shard arrivals: max(floor, 2.6 - 0.005*dl) where the floor decays from 0.80 at dl 340 to 0.50 at dl 965.
detail: floor = max(0.50, 0.80 - max(0,d-340)*0.00048). Written as max(floor, ramp) rather than min(ramp, floor): the first draft used a min, which let the decaying term undercut the opening ramp and pulled level 4's opening gap from 0.90 to 0.85 — a difficulty change smuggled into the window the change promised not to touch. The two lines cross at dl 362, so everything below that is bit-identical to what shipped. Arrival rate is the lever the board actually feels, more than the cap.

name: firstShardAt / rookie
summary: The opening calm: the first shard is held 4.5s + 8.5s*rookie(), so run one opens at 13.0s and run four at 4.5s.
detail: rookie() = max(0, min(1,(4-G.runs)/3), min(1,(G.struggle||0)/3)) — run count OR the struggle streak, whichever asks for more calm, so three consecutive sub-30s deaths reopen the full opening no matter how many lifetime runs the counter shows. startGame increments G.runs before play, so run 1 sees rookie()=1 and a 13.0s hold; the adjacent comment still says 11s and is stale. Replaced a flat 7s floor that charged every returning player ten seconds of dead air.

name: emberCap / emberGap
summary: Ember supply scales with ring count: cap = min(12, round((3.5+dl*0.004)*nRings)), gap = max(0.30, (1.35-dl*0.003)/nRings).
detail: Both scale with G.nRings because an ember lands on a random ring but is only collectable on the one you are riding — without the scaling, adding a ring silently cuts scoring rate while raising difficulty. Raising the 12 cap floods the board; raising the 0.30 gap floor starves the combo and the build meter.

name: shieldMax
summary: The shield bank grows with the clock: 3 below dl 160, 4 below dl 320, 5 thereafter, plus mode.shields (0 for skill).
detail: Three slots stopped being enough to play around once the board reached three rings and the inner ring cost twice the angle per shard. MODES.skill.shields is 0 — the additive knob is the one knob whose identity element is zero rather than one, which check.mjs's mode-derivation guard knows about.

name: CW / WARN / FADE / HOP
summary: Four core timings: 2.5s combo window, 1.15s fallback shard warn, 0.4s shard fade-out, 0.14s ring hop (0.49s on menus).
detail: WARN is only the default when a spike carries no warn of its own — mkSpike stamps warnTime() at spawn, so WARN is effectively a floor for hand-made spikes such as the menu demo's. FADE is how long a phase-2 (harmless) shard lingers before splice. HOP is the ring transition duration; menu, swipe-select, level-select and power-select screens run it at HOP*3.5. CW is the seconds an ember chain stays alive.

name: LAP_EMB_MAX / orbit payout
summary: An orbit pays 6 + 13 per fed ember up to four (max 58), plus a fed-streak bonus of 7 per streak step capped at 28.
detail: LAP_EMB_MAX=4 is the number of embers per orbit that still raise the payout; a fifth pays nothing extra. The streak bonus saturates at five laps. Total ceiling is 86, which is the figure the nova comment compares against when arguing that converting shards in place paid almost nothing. The streak is deliberately NOT rendered as a multiplier — the house style reserves 'NOUN xN' for multipliers and this is base+bonus.

name: TIERS
summary: The 13-rung formation ladder from dl 0 to dl 610, each rung a spawn type or a ring count plus the banner line that announces it.
detail: Rungs: 0 single; 12 SECOND RING (2 rings); 18 TWIN SHARDS; 40 THIRD RING (3 rings); 100 GATES; 128 DRIFTERS; 165 BLINKERS; 240 SLIDING GATES; 275 THE SAUCER; 310 FLICKER PAIRS; 395 DIVERS; 520 THE NARROWS; 610 THE EYE. There is no rung at dl 340 any more — THE EYE moved to level 6's floor, so levels 4 and 5 open with no banner at their own floor. Every `sub` is word-for-word its type's MEET lesson — smoke.mjs diffs them and fails on drift. smoke.mjs also pins the last rung's `at` to the last level's floor and asserts `at` is non-decreasing. tierIndex() holds the ladder at SECOND RING until the first hop, with a 30-difficulty-second release valve, so the exam waits for the lesson.

name: T_VOICE / T_SKY
summary: The tier indices the band and the sky answer to, derived by NAME from TIERS rather than hardcoded, so inserting a rung costs nothing.
detail: T_VOICE = [0, index of THIRD RING, index of BLINKERS, index of THE EYE]; T_SKY = [0, index of GATES, index of SLIDING GATES, index of THE EYE]. Both findIndex on `name`, so a RENAMED row fails loudly in check.mjs instead of quietly re-timing the audio ladder. Twelve places used to hardcode ordinals; inserting DIVERS and THE NARROWS moved THE EYE, so every `G.tier>=10` silently stopped meaning 'the last rung'. Resolved against the current 13-row table: T_VOICE = [0,3,6,12] and T_SKY = [0,4,7,12] — the band's and the sky's top rungs are both THE EYE at dl 610.

name: SHAPE_RANK
summary: How much reading each formation asks for (0 single to 4 compound), used only by the late-board weighting in pickType above dl 340.
detail: Ranked by independent facts the player must read before knowing what to do: a single is a position; a twin is a position and a count; a gate is a wall and a verb; a diver is a position that CHANGES; the compounds are two behaviours at once, and the saucer is the only shape whose position is a function of the player's own choices. Nothing reads this below dl 340, so it cannot affect the tuned first three levels.

name: LV
summary: Six levels with difficulty-clock windows 0-90, 90-215, 215-340, 340-470, 470-610, 610-Infinity, each with a key scalar and a two-or-three-line card.
detail: Names: LIFT OFF, INTO THE RINGS, THE STORM, EVENT HORIZON, REDSHIFT, HEAT DEATH. `key` scales PENT and walks the whole-tone scale down (1, 0.8909, 0.7937, 0.7071, 0.6300, 0.5612) — six whole steps, one full lap, which is why there are six levels. Level 6's `end` is Infinity because it is the authored frontier, not an endless-mode rule. `mech` rows are checked against MECHANICS.md and against the MEET lessons; a null sub is resolved at draw time by swipeWords(). Level 1 gets three lines, the rest two, because a card that previews the syllabus competes with the banner and lesson that teach each thing at the moment it arrives.

name: MODES
summary: The difficulty table, currently one row: skill is the identity element — every knob 1, except the additive shields knob at 0.
detail: Knobs are clock, speed, warn, cap, gap, shields, demo. check.mjs fails the build if a knob stops being neutral on skill, if a row has different knobs from skill, or if a knob is declared without a call site. CHILL was retired to one row deliberately and the mechanism kept, because the rule it encodes — a second difficulty is a DERIVATIVE, never a second implementation — was arrived at rather than obvious. The clock knob is the main lever; the rest are trims on top of it. A mode may never touch the curriculum, the music or the scoring.

name: LAB_DL
summary: The powerup lab pins the difficulty clock at dl 40 forever — exactly TIERS[3].at, the lowest value that gives the arena all three orbits.
detail: Three rings matter because the black hole opens a FOURTH on entry and restores what it found on exit, so a one-ring lab would have demonstrated that reveal against nothing. dl 40 buys shard cap 4 over three rings, a 2.4s arrival gap, speed 1.62 of a 4.2 ceiling, and a 2.35s telegraph. Level 1's finish line is dl 90 and the clock never moves, so the lab is endless. smoke.mjs asserts dl()===LAB_DL and derives the calm-board shard cap from it rather than hardcoding, and fails if that cap exceeds 5.

name: LAB_ORBS
summary: The lab picker's ten rows, in order: shield, warp, nova, spot, hyper, mirror, scorch, slip, trail, blackhole, with LAB.sel defaulting to index 5.
detail: Every description is lifted verbatim from the channel that already explains that orb — hintText for the three intro orbs, MEET for the ones that carry lessons — so the picker cannot drift into being a second, differently-worded description of the same things. smoke.mjs compares the drawn rows against LAB_ORBS ids and plays every row for 45 seconds; check.mjs collects mechanic names from TIERS and LAB_ORBS for the ledger-drift guard against MECHANICS.md. Note the default LAB.sel of 5 selects 'mirror', not the blackhole named in LAB.type.

name: PAUSE_COUNT / PAUSE_COOL
summary: Pause resumes after a 3-second frozen visible countdown, and cannot re-arm until 5 seconds of real play have passed.
detail: Pause is a FLAG, not a state: G.state stays 'playing' (a 'paused' state would have rendered GAME OVER over a live run, since draw() dispatches with the death screen as its final else) and what stops is the clock — update() returns before G.t+=dt, freezing every deadline in the file at once. The board is HIDDEN while paused because a button that freezes a 1-2.35s telegraph mid-flight is a difficulty change wearing a convenience label; the cooldown closes the pause-resume-pause loophole that would rebuild the same free look. The bed is taken down explicitly on the way in, because a stopped bedTick freezes the pad droning one chord rather than silencing it.

name: BLINK / BDUTY
summary: A blinker's cycle is exactly two beats (SPB*2 = 1.154s) and a lone blinker is armed 55% of it; a flicker pair overrides duty to 0.5.
detail: Two beats rather than the arbitrary 1.15s it replaced — within 4ms of the same feel, but now on the grid. A pair is offset by exactly half a cycle, so at 0.55 duty BOTH sides were armed for 10% of every cycle while the lesson promised 'only one is solid at a time'. At duty 0.5 exactly one side is lethal at every instant and the sentence holds literally. smoke.mjs samples 120 points of the cycle and fails if both or neither are armed.

name: SAUCER_LAG / CHG / BEAM / HOP / COOL
summary: The saucer holds 0.55 rad off the tail, charges one beat, blocks its ring for 0.42s, follows a hop after 0.42s, and waits 9-15s between visits.
detail: The body is never solid — only the shot is. A solid object pinned behind the comet would be lethal on the same frame as the tap, turning every reflexive reversal into a death with no move against it. So it threatens on a CLOCK: harmless while you travel, and when you turn back it charges for SAUCER_CHG (one beat, so the shot lands in the bar) before blocking. The answer always exists because it is still on the ring you LEFT and takes SAUCER_HOP to follow. Without the cooldown its measured uptime was 45-57% of level 4; SAUCER_COOL holds it to roughly a quarter of the run.

name: DEMO
summary: The title-screen demo runs a 12-second loop: a shard at 1s, a reversal at 2.8s, a hop inward at 6s and a hop back out at 9s.
detail: Drawn by the menu branch of drawHUD off the same clock, so the ghost glyphs and the demo action are one thing. startGame resets everything it touches. Shortening the loop makes the menu busier; the beats are spaced so a newcomer can watch each verb answered by the actual object before touching the screen.

name: UPG
summary: Eleven upgrade tiles drafted three at a time on the calm card between levels; taken tiles never repeat, declined ones may re-enter.
detail: Tiles: longstar (hypernova ~14s), deepbank (3 shields at level start), slowworld (slow-mo 9s), richnova (2 stars per cleared red), hairtrig (starfall after two fed orbits), stagelight (magnet 16s), longmirror (mirror ~14s), deepburn (scorch 13s), steadyhand (wider tap window), longslip (slipstream 18s, minLevel 2), longtrail (star trail 24s, minLevel 3). They are UPGRADES, never new orbs, so the curriculum rule survives the draft intact. The `!G.offered` filter used to burn every unpicked tile for the whole run, which starved the level-5 and level-6 cards; declined tiles now re-enter once the fresh pool runs thin. check.mjs parses the UPG literal for ids and asserts each is wired.

name: BH_DUR
summary: The black hole lasts 17 seconds end to end; staying past it loses the bank and a shield.
detail: The full rarity clock armed on entry is 55 seconds, chosen so a 17s mode leaves ~38s of quiet after it. smoke.mjs drives BH.t=BH_DUR-0.1 to test the too-late branch, and check.mjs's doc-staleness guard requires any docs paragraph naming BH_DUR to state 17.

name: BH_ESCAPE
summary: Gravity releases at 12 seconds — the ESCAPE call — leaving 5 seconds to reach the outermost ring before the wager is lost.
detail: At BH_ESCAPE the banner clears, 'ESCAPE: swipe to the outer ring' is said, a cue sounds, and no fresh wall may close behind the signal. bhDensity also ramps 1.25 to 2.00 linearly over BH.t/BH_ESCAPE during the challenge phase, so pressure peaks exactly as the escape opens.

name: BH_WARP
summary: The opening phase takes 0.85 seconds to warp in; at warp 1 the mode enters phase 2 and the fourth ring appears.
detail: BH.warp = min(1, BH.t/BH_WARP) during phase 1 and is read by the shader as the black hole's accent strength. smoke.mjs advances exactly bhTick(BH_WARP) to reach the challenge phase, so shortening it does not break the harness but lengthening it delays every subsequent assertion by the same amount.

name: BH_TS
summary: Time scale inside the black hole: 0.60 during the challenge, 0.372 (0.60*0.62) while it opens; ordinary slow-mo is 0.55.
detail: tsT = bhActive() ? (BH.phase===1 ? BH_TS*0.62 : BH_TS) : (G.slow>0 ? 0.55 : 1). This scales G.vt, the presentation clock, so the backdrop, the camera dolly and the arena all dilate together — slow motion used to reach the simulation and stop there. G.t is never dilated, so every deadline in the file stays in real seconds.

name: BH_DENSITY / bhDensity
summary: Shard density multiplier during the black hole: a flat 1.25 outside the challenge phase, ramping 1.25 to 2.00 across the 12s to ESCAPE.
detail: bhDensity() = BH.phase===2 ? 1.25+0.75*min(1, BH.t/BH_ESCAPE) : BH_DENSITY. It multiplies shardCap and DIVIDES spawnGap, so cap and arrival rate move together — raising one without the other only changes how long the board takes to fill. Note the ramp hardcodes 1.25 and 0.75 rather than reading BH_DENSITY, so changing BH_DENSITY alone changes only the non-challenge value.

name: BH_PULL / BH_IGNITE
summary: Gravity pulls the player one ring outward every 4 seconds of not moving inward, and an ignition lights for 1.2 seconds when it fires.
detail: BH.pullT accumulates and fires at BH_PULL when the hop has settled (G.hopP>=1). The last second before it fires is drawn as a brightening ellipse on the outer ring (BH.pullT > BH_PULL-1), so the pull is telegraphed rather than sprung. smoke.mjs asserts BH.pullT resets — a completed orbit used to leave it accumulating past BH_PULL forever.

name: BH_HORIZON
summary: The maximum bank a black hole can pay is 600 points from eight seconds at the inner ring; the escape bonus is (80 + 600*charge + 20*stars) halved-ish per shield spent.
detail: bonus = round((80 + BH_HORIZON*BH.charge + 20*BH.score) / 1.5^min(3,spent)). BH.charge is the normalised bank; BH.score counts stars taken inside the mode. smoke.mjs uses BH_HORIZON as the yardstick for 'the wager did not pay twice', asserting the score gain stays under another BH_HORIZON.

name: MAGNET_RANGE / MAGNET_SECS / MAGNET_FLIGHT
summary: The magnet captures stars within 110 scale units on the current ring or an adjacent one, for 10 seconds, each flying in over 0.38s.
detail: Capture requires abs(s.ring - effRing()) <= 1. A captured star follows a quadratic Bezier whose control point bends by min(22, d*0.28) in the travel direction, so the flight curves rather than snapping. Coordinates are stored in scale units around the hub so a resize cannot strand a captured star. The LONG MAGNET upgrade (stagelight) raises the duration to 16s. Only MAGNET_RANGE is caught by the doc-staleness guard; MAGNET_SECS and MAGNET_FLIGHT are later names in the same declaration and are invisible to it.

name: NOVA_SP
summary: The nova front expands at 560 scale units per second, or fast enough to clear the ring system in 0.62s on a large viewport, whichever is faster.
detail: sp = max(NOVA_SP*u, (2R+60u)/0.62). The old 1600 was picked to clear a screen diagonal, but no shard is ever on the diagonal — every one sits inside the ring system, so the cascade finished in thirteen frames and the front then expanded through empty space. 560 puts the same sweep at ~0.65s on a phone. The viewport-derived floor exists because on a big screen the player could otherwise die inside their own blast when the front outran the invulnerability window. Blast starts at radius 34u.

name: MIRROR_BEATS
summary: The mirror runs sixteen beats (9.23s at 104bpm), or twenty-four with the LONG MIRROR upgrade; it collects stars exactly opposite the comet.
detail: Measured in beats, in the same unit as the hypernova and the spotlight, so it lands on the grid rather than on a stopwatch. Its angle is derived every frame as G.angle+PI — a reflection, not a chaser. It collects stars and converts armed shards on the player's own ring only, ignoring trail stars (the offered route belongs to the player) and magnet-captured ones. It was named THE MIRROR rather than THE TWIN because TWIN SHARDS is already a formation; ECHO is a banned string that check.mjs fails the build on.

name: SCORCH_SECS / BURN_SECT / BURN_LIFE
summary: Scorch burns your wake for 8 seconds (13 upgraded); the burn is stored as 72 sectors per ring, each lit for at least 2.6 seconds.
detail: Sectors rather than a list of arcs, because sectors cannot overlap, cannot leak, and cost one array. Each painted sector's life is max(BURN_LIFE, TAU/max(0.3,G.speed)+0.2) so at least one full orbit of wake is always visible, including on the lab's slower board, and it is stored in gameplay seconds so slow motion does not erase it. Anything red standing in or arming into a lit sector is converted. Only SCORCH_SECS is visible to the doc-staleness guard.

name: SLIP_SECS / SLIP_ARC / SLIP_GRACE / SLIP_COOL
summary: Slipstream lasts 12 seconds (18 upgraded); each ring change clears red within 0.48 rad, grants 0.4s of grace and arms a 0.8s cooldown.
detail: On a hop it converts every non-saucer shard on the destination ring within SLIP_ARC of the player's angle, then sets G.invuln to at least now+SLIP_GRACE and G.slipAt to now+SLIP_COOL. The cooldown is what stops a rapid hop chain clearing the whole board. Only SLIP_SECS is visible to the doc-staleness guard.

name: STAR_ROUTE_N / STAR_ROUTE_SECS / STAR_ROUTE_BONUS
summary: The star trail lays nine bonus stars, alive 16 seconds (24 upgraded), each paying +4 on top of the combo.
detail: Stars are laid at G.angle + dir*(0.62 + i*0.62) alternating between the current ring and an adjacent one in the direction already travelled. It is a reward to pursue, not a safe lane: reds remain. A later pickup replaces the previous route rather than piling routes up. Trail stars are excluded from the mirror's automatic collection — the offered route belongs to the player.

name: orb pickup durations (one table)
summary: Every orb's live duration in one place: slow-mo 6s (9 upgraded), magnet 10s (16), mirror 16 beats (24), scorch 8s (13), slipstream 12s (18), trail 16s (24), hypernova 16 beats (24).
detail: The beat-measured orbs (mirror, hypernova) multiply SPB, so a tempo change retimes them; the second-measured ones do not. Each upgraded value is a literal at the pickup site rather than a named constant, which is why editing e.g. SCORCH_SECS alone leaves the DEEP BURN tile's 13 seconds untouched — and the UPG tile's own description string is a third copy that must be edited with it. The black hole is not on this list: it runs BH_DUR.

name: POWPOOL
summary: The post-intro orb roll: shield .302, warp .185, nova .143, spot .134, slip .095, trail .095, mirror .080, scorch .080, hyper .076, each with a level floor.
detail: Declared INSIDE spawnPow rather than at module scope, so it is rebuilt on every roll and cannot be inspected from the console. Level floors are shield/warp/nova 1, hyper/slip 2, spot/trail 3, mirror 4, scorch 5; the weights are renormalised over whichever rows the current level admits, which keeps every surviving ratio exact. Two cut orbs (magnetar, bass bomb) had their shares redistributed proportionally by the same rule. Rolls only happen after the intro trio, the pity shield (sinceShield>=3) and the level guarantees have all declined.

name: POW_INTRO / POW_LESSON / orb placement
summary: Every run opens with shield, slow-mo and nova in that order; after three non-shield placements a pity shield is forced, and an orb lives 7 seconds.
detail: The trio replays per RUN, not per level. G.introN advances on PLACEMENT, not pickup, so a player who misses the slow-mo still advances the curriculum — otherwise a run spent dodging would serve nothing but shields forever. A pity shield placed while the trio still owes one counts as the trio's shield. POW_LESSON maps each later orb to the once-per-device flag that marks its first-encounter lesson as spent. A declined black hole arms a 20s cooldown rather than the full 55s.

name: dropNeed / build
summary: Starfall is earned from three star-fed orbits, or two with the EARLY STARFALL upgrade; nothing else fills the meter.
detail: build() ignores every source except 'orbit' with amount >= 0.04, and refuses entirely during an intro, the lab, the black hole, the finale or an active starfall. On reaching dropNeed the meter resets, G.dropsEarned increments, and armDrop('STARFALL','orbit') fires if the audio context is running — otherwise startStarfall() runs directly, so a muted or blocked-audio game still gets its reward. This is the player-facing contract CLAUDE.md states in as many words.

name: BUILD_SRC / DROP_STEP
summary: The build meter's four source labels survive, but DROP_STEP and DROP_STEP_MAX are both 0 and read nowhere — the meter now only counts orbits.
detail: BUILD_SRC maps ember/hop/time/orbit to the on-screen reasons GATHERING SPARKS, WORKING THE RINGS, PLAYING IN TIME and CLEAN ORBITS. Its surrounding comment argues at length for a meter filled by everything the game considers playing well, which is no longer what build() does: three of the four sources are rejected at the guard. DROP_STEP and DROP_STEP_MAX appear exactly once each in the repository.

name: LAND_WIN / LAND_PERFECT
summary: LAND_WIN (0.29) survives only as the count-in ring's early bound; LAND_PERFECT (0.12) and tryLand() are retired.
detail: tryLand() is an empty function with the comment 'a reward never asks for a different tap'. LAND_WIN's one remaining reader is the count-in visual: cin = (cd > -LAND_WIN && cd < SPB*4) ? 1-max(0,cd)/(SPB*4) : 0, which makes the comet's own ring swell white-hot through the final bar before a drop lands. LAND_PERFECT has no reader at all.

name: SWIPE_MODE / swipeOut / swipeWords
summary: Two swipe rules, chosen once by the player: 'radial' (default) reads out from the hub, 'screen' makes up always outer and down always inner.
detail: swipeOut() is the ONLY place either rule is expressed, and both gesture-resolution paths call it, so they cannot drift apart. The radial normal at parametric angle a is (cos a, AY sin a), not (cos a, sin a) — on a stretched arena the pure basis reads a vertical flick near the top of the loop as barely radial at all. swipeWords() returns the matching sentence, and five channels (menu key, level 1 card, SECOND RING banner, hint ladder, death coach) all read it rather than hardcoding 'swipe up or down'. smoke.mjs drives both modes through swipeOut and compares the two sentences.

name: RADIAL_MIN / swipe commit
summary: A pointer move under 32px is not a gesture; RADIAL_MIN 0.34 (~20 degrees off tangential) is how far it must lean before it counts as a ring change.
detail: A tap fires a speculative reverse immediately (direction flips instantly, effects wait REV_FX), and crossing the swipe threshold rolls that reverse back — including didReverse, so a run whose only 'reverse' was speculative does not count one. The reference angle is where the comet was when the gesture started, which is what the player was actually looking at when they committed.

name: REV_FX
summary: A tap's sound and sparks wait 0.07 seconds so a gesture that turns out to be a swipe stays silent.
detail: The direction flip itself is instant — only the effects are delayed. This is what makes the speculative-reverse-then-roll-back design inaudible. Raising it makes taps feel laggy; lowering it lets every swipe start with a reverse chirp.

name: GEST
summary: Gesture outcome counters (tap, swipe, lateSwipe, unresolved), counted where each resolves and deliberately not inside bump().
detail: bump() also fires when a swipe hits the outermost or innermost ring, which is the game answering correctly rather than a misread — counting there would have inflated the misread rate. These feed telemetry rather than gameplay.

name: ANN / annPump
summary: One announcement at a time: 2.8 seconds between lines, a 14-second default shelf life, and a banner younger than 2.6s blocks the queue.
detail: Six systems used to write the announcement slot directly with unconditional overwrites, so 'NEW LAYER: BASS' could eat 'GOLDEN LAP' while its 13-second window kept running with its only explanation destroyed. say() enqueues with a priority and a TTL, never queuing a duplicate string; a message that expires unshown is dropped rather than shouted late. sayNow() bypasses the queue for the two bar-timed section calls whose whole meaning is the instant they refer to.

name: flashHit rate limit
summary: Small screen flashes (under 0.5) rate-limit to one every 0.45 seconds; big moments always pass.
detail: Seven systems max() into G.flash, which at mid-game density strobed the screen near-continuously. The 0.5 cut is what keeps a perfect landing and a nova unconditional while the routine hits queue behind each other.

name: popup cap
summary: At most four floating score popups at once; the oldest yields, and survivors dim by age so the eye lands on the newest.
detail: Six was a cap on the crash, not on the noise: screenshotted in the finale, four identical '+60' floated in a column at equal weight, none of them the news. Four still lets a nova cascade read as a cascade.

name: PIPDT
summary: 0.16 seconds between two level pips landing on the death screen, read by the reveal, the LEVEL punch-in and the input lockout.
detail: One constant with three readers, so the punch-in that waits for the last pip and the lockout that waits for all three cannot disagree. The pip bar draws LEVEL_MAX diamonds, filled up to G.level.

name: CLOUD_ORIGIN
summary: The optional cloud save and leaderboard live at https://cosmo-arcade.netlify.app; the merge is done on the server, not here.
detail: Two devices on one account means two writers, so netlify/lib/records.mjs takes the max of each record rather than letting the last writer win — which is also why the client can post without reading first: it cannot lower anything. The credential lives in localStorage under cometloop:auth. Accounts remain optional and native assets work offline.

name: POSTHOG_KEY / POSTHOG_HOST / TELE_OK / TELE_ID
summary: Telemetry posts straight to PostHog US with no SDK; TELE_OK silences file:// and localhost, and TELE_ID is one random per-device id.
detail: Deliberately no SDK and no third-party script tag: nothing to load, so no load order to get wrong and no loader to fail silently. The key is a write-only project token, safe in a public file. No autocapture, no session recording, no cookies, no names. sendBeacon first (survives the tab closing mid-death), keepalive fetch as fallback; a blocked network is silently ignored. The device id lives at cometloop:pid, and private mode falls back to a per-visit id. Lab runs are silent at the track() call rather than by tagging.

name: BLOOM_DIV / BLOOM_ALPHA
summary: Bloom is drawn into a quarter-size buffer and composited at 0.28 alpha, never read back from the main canvas.
detail: The obvious route — drawImage(cv) into a small buffer — measures ~16ms a frame because pulling 1.3M pixels back stalls the pipeline. Instead the bright objects are re-drawn as crude blobs into the 1/BLOOM_DIV buffer; precision is pointless there because the bilinear upscale IS the blur. The composite alpha is multiplied by 1+0.45*G.beat during a payoff section. Raising BLOOM_DIV shrinks the buffer and widens the blur while cheapening the pass.

name: HALO_DIV / HALO_WDIV / HALO_K1 / HALO_W1 / HALO_K2 / HALO_W2 / HALO_A / HALO_WA
summary: The 2D halo: two extra discs per light at 2x weight 0.50 and 4x weight 0.20, into 1/12 and 1/32 buffers, composited at 0.09 and 0.06.
detail: HALO_A and HALO_WA are `let` so `HALO_A=0.14` in the console re-weights the glow on the next frame — the last word on how much glow is too much belongs to eyes on a real screen. Real circles rather than a mip cascade: a box downsample preserves the peak of any feature bigger than a buffer pixel, so the passes simply SUM (the core came out 61% hotter while the halo barely moved), and a tiny buffer blown up 40x spreads through a bilinear tent whose footprint is a cross, not a disc — sliding one ember across a coarse pixel swung its halo by 80%. Measured as set: ember core +4.8%, reach x3.6, on a 390x844 phone ember 15px -> 54px and comet 22px -> 78px.

name: FX_A / FX_MIDW / FX_WIDEW / FX_SPREAD / FX_AB
summary: The GPU glow chain: composite alpha 0.55, mid and wide level weights 0.62 and 0.85, a 1.15-texel blur step and 0.0045 of radial aberration.
detail: FX_A is `let` and mutable at runtime for the same reason HALO_A is. FX_SPREAD at 1.6 reaches further but starts showing the five taps — the hub's roundness falls 0.881 to 0.821. FX_AB is quoted as the R-to-B sample separation it produces on an 844px screen: 0 at the arena centre, 1.14px at 0.5H idle, 3.80px running hot, 7.60px in the black hole. Zero at the centre by construction, so the fringe never touches the orbits the player is reading. When the FX chain is on it replaces the two 2D halo blits entirely; only the tight bloom buffer is still composited over it. fxcheck.mjs reads FX_SPREAD out of the source text.

name: RING_LIT
summary: Four stacked arcs light the comet's own track: half-widths 0.62/0.40/0.22/0.10 rad at alphas 0.030/0.048/0.078/0.105 and widths 7/4.5/2.6/1.6u.
detail: Each entry is [half-angle, alpha, lineWidth in u]. Drawn with 'lighter' composite in the current ring's own RINGS[].tint, so the light under the comet says which ring you are on as plainly as the arrangement does. Every alpha is multiplied by 1+0.30*G.beat unless reduced motion is on. Decorative, but load-bearing for the 'which ring am I on' read.

name: GL_SCALE
summary: The sky shader renders at full resolution (1.0) with no performance downgrade ladder; the adaptive version described in implementation.md is gone.
detail: The comment is one line: 'fixed quality; no performance downgrade'. docs/engine/implementation.md still describes a dial that starts at 0.60 and rises toward 1.0 with a latching ceiling and a raise fed only by gameplay frames — that whole mechanism no longer exists in the runtime. The doc passes check.mjs only because the same paragraph happens to contain the literal 1.0.

name: GL_MOTION
summary: 0.25 on the integrated scenic clock — the sky's drift rate, and never a beat gain; one of the two renderer controls CLAUDE.md names.
detail: Multiplied by each world's own `motion` field (0.48 to 0.80 across WORLDS), so the effective dial varies by destination. Raising it makes the backdrop move faster and risks the motion that failed playtesting at 1.0 — undirected drift of everything, meaning nothing. implementation.md discusses a historical 0.42 -> 0.72 in one paragraph and states the current 0.25 in another. It is deliberately not driven by the beat: glRipple() and glShear() are empty stubs, because a tap or an ordinary beat distorting the whole sky was removed.

name: F (font stack) / fitSz
summary: A geometric-sans stack led by Avenir Next, with fitSz shrinking any line to fit its width and never below 8u.
detail: The old stack led with -apple-system, so on the target device every word was San Francisco — the system UI face, which reads as a settings screen rather than a game. Every family here ships with some OS, so there is no font to download and no network call. fitSz reserves letterSpacing before measuring, because the draw adds it AFTER measureText sees the string; without that reservation a tracked line still overflows.

name: RM (prefers-reduced-motion)
summary: One boolean read once at load from prefers-reduced-motion, gating the beat boosts, the comet flicker, the sky drift and the scene accent entirely.
detail: Read at module scope, so a mid-session OS change does not take effect until reload. Its readers include: RING_LIT's beat boost, the bloom composite's beat boost, FLK's comet flicker (constant 0.6 / 0.5 instead), skyStep's vt (pinned to 0), skyArtPlate's camera drift, sceneAccent (returns quiet unconditionally), and several hit-stop and shake sites. A muted, offline or reduced-motion game still works — that is a stated player-facing contract.

name: COL
summary: The closed colour vocabulary: cyan comet, gold ember, pink-red shard, mint shield, violet warp, white nova, magenta hypernova, violet-blue black hole, blue mirror, orange scorch.
detail: One colour per meaning and the list is closed: cyan = you, gold = earned, violet = the music, pink-red = death and death only, mint = shield, white = the peak. Everything past that is an ORB's identity and is spent on that orb alone. The hypernova was COL.ember — the exact gold of the collectible stars — so 'am I invincible' was signalled in the one colour already meaning 'points'; magenta at ~318deg is the furthest usable hue from ember (~42deg) and shard (~352deg). Scorch is deliberately warm-ORANGE rather than warm-red because red belongs to death alone and #ff5d73 is a pink.

name: BUILD / IN_APP_BROWSER
summary: BUILD is the Vite-injected commit stamp (falling back to 'dev'); a range request on the live file compares it and self-updates from the menu.
detail: The updater fetches the first 8KB of the deployed file, matches /const BUILD='([0-9a-f]{7})'/, and if the hash differs and G.state==='menu' calls location.replace with ?u=<hash>. It only ever acts on the menu, so a live run is never reloaded under the player. IN_APP_BROWSER is a separate load-time sniff used for the environments where audio unlock and fullscreen behave differently.
